reason: E2 directly supports the hardness and intermetallic formation premises for CoCrFeMnNiTi0.75 on steel, but the hypothesis extends these to TC4 without evidence. E1 shows laser cladding on TC4 can produce sound coatings, but for different refractory alloys, not CoCrFeMnNi. No cited evidence addresses friction reduction by Ti addition, bonding quality of this specific coating on TC4, or preservation of TC4's properties.
premises: CoCrFeMnNiTi0.75 coating achieves high hardness (511 HV) on 40Cr steel via laser cladding
Ti addition >0.5 molar ratio forms Fe2Ti, Ni3Ti, Co2Ti intermetallics in CoCrFeMnNi
Laser cladding can produce defect-free, strongly bonded coatings on Ti alloys
Ti addition reduces friction coefficient in CoCrFeMnNi coatings
CoCrFeMnNi-based coatings can be transferred to TC4 without compromising substrate properties
